title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: PLAC — habitus not sensible; spiritual death effects
pass_a_gloss: For habits are not sensible qualities, nor are they sensed or understood by us, except insofar as from antecedent or consequent acts they are detected to be present. Add that spiritual death, as far as true piety is concerned, deprives the man of sense and of the faculty of acting well, and makes him unfit for every good work, prone to every evil, turned away from God, but turned toward the flesh and those things which God hates.
pass_b_english: Habits are not sensible qualities. We neither feel nor understand them except as we infer them from acts that go before or follow. Add this: spiritual death, for true piety, strips a man of sense and of the power to do well. It makes him unfit for every good work, ready for every evil, turned from God, and turned to the flesh and to what God hates.
source_text: Habitus enim non sunt qualitates sensibiles, neque sentiuntur, aut intelliguntur a nobis, nisi quatenus ex antecedentibus aut consequentibus actibus inesse deprehenduntur. Adde quod mors spiritualis, quantum ad veram pietatem attinet, hominem sensu privat, & facultate bene agendi, eumque ad omne bonum opus ineptum, ad omne malum pronum, aversum a Deo, conversum autem ad carnem & ea quae Deus odit, efficit.

choices.choice: habitus not sensible; spiritual death blinds and disables
